transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I have an overwhelming, intense fear of enclosed spaces, especially elevators and airplanes. It has gotten really difficult to deal with, so I'm hoping to get some help for it.

When you’re in or anticipating enclosed spaces like elevators or airplanes, do you mainly fear having panic-like symptoms or being unable to escape, or is the fear focused on the enclosed space itself?

My fear is definitely focused on the enclosed spaces themselves and the terrifying feeling of being trapped inside them. I don't really worry about having a panic attack or finding a safe place; it's just the physical, tight space of the elevator or plane that scares me.
Do you avoid elevators, airplanes, or other enclosed spaces because of this fear, and has it significantly interfered with your work, travel, or daily life?

Yes, I avoid them at all costs; I'll walk up ten flights of stairs just to stay out of an elevator. I also refuse to fly, which has severely limited my travel plans and even caused major issues with my job. It has really disrupted my daily life.
How long have you had this fear of enclosed spaces, and has it been present for at least 6 months?
I've been dealing with this intense fear for about a year and eleven months now. So yes, it has definitely been going on for much longer than six months.
